builtOn.calendar.text: AI 2027 is the fast case; its authors now expect it later. Here dates move with the pace.
builtOn.scenarios.0.what: AI improving itself by late 2027, told through two fictional labs.
builtOn.scenarios.1.what: five worlds, from an AI plateau to an arms race; ten endings.
builtOn.scenarios.2.what: Europe squeezed between the US and China unless it acts.
builtOn.tagsText: Every news item says where it comes from:
builtOn.title: Built on three scenarios
card.ai_office.example: Under the AI Act, the European Commission’s AI Office has “the ability to conduct evaluations of GPAI models”.
card.ai_office.name: Hire testers for the AI Office
card.ai_office.proposal: The EU’s AI Office already has the power to test big AI models. This gives it the people: testers paid like lab engineers, with their own computers. They halve what you don’t know about the labs’ claims and sharpen every inspection. If AI starts thinking in a code no one can read, they keep testing what it does.
card.ai_office.short: Hire top testers so the AI Office can check the labs’ claims.
card.ai_office.text: Hire top AI testers for the AI Office. You check far more of the labs’ claims, even when AI thinking turns unreadable. Other budgets pay.
card.ai_office.why: Paying testers like lab engineers squeezes other budgets.
card.alignment.costLine: In July 2025, the UK’s AI Security Institute launched a fund of over £15 million for alignment research.
card.alignment.name: Fund AI safety research
card.alignment.proposal: Europe funds independent teams in universities working on alignment: making AI reliably do what we intend. Their papers are public, but the big labs use little of them on their own. Once an inspection accord opens the labs to European teams, their work counts for far more. Most of it never shows in the labs’ reports. Other budgets pay.
card.alignment.short: Pay independent teams to work on making AI safe.
card.alignment.text: Pay independent teams to work on making AI safe. The labs adopt little of it unless inspectors give your teams access.
card.alignment.ups.0: AI safety shown: up a little
card.alignment.ups.1: Real safety up (not shown), more with an accord
card.alignment.why: Labs rarely use outside research unless inspectors get in.
card.asml.example: The Europe 2031 report: “The only card Europe still holds is ASML - the one bottleneck the entire AI race runs through.”
card.asml.failure: The lever failed: US export rules, not Europe, decide where ASML may sell.
card.asml.name: Bargain with ASML’s chip machines
card.asml.options.access.name: Trade chip machines for AI access
card.asml.options.access.proposal: Every advanced chip needs ASML’s chip-printing machines, and the Dutch government decides, with Washington, who may buy them. Europe uses that leverage: no new machines unless the AI labs let European firms and public services use their newest models. Washington won’t let Europe set terms: expect it to block European chip-tool sales to China.
card.asml.options.access.short: ASML sells chip machines only if EU firms get the labs’ models.
card.asml.options.safety.name: Trade chip machines for safety tests
card.asml.options.safety.proposal: Every advanced chip needs ASML’s chip-printing machines, and the Dutch government decides, with Washington, who may buy them. Europe uses that leverage: no new machines unless the AI labs open their newest models to European testers. Washington won’t let Europe set terms: expect it to block European chip-tool sales to China.
card.asml.options.safety.short: ASML sells chip machines only if labs let EU testers check models.
card.asml.proposal: Every advanced chip needs ASML’s chip-printing machines, and the Dutch government decides, with Washington, who may buy them. Europe pushes for that leverage: ask the labs to open their newest models to European testers, or to give European firms and public services access. Washington won’t let Europe set terms: expect it to block European chip-tool sales to China.
card.asml.short: Tie ASML’s chip-machine sales to a deal with the AI labs.
card.asml.text: ASML, a Dutch firm, alone makes the machines for the best chips. Tie their sales to a deal: labs give way; Washington hits back.
card.asml.ups.0: AI safety: more verified, or cohesion up some
card.asml.why: Washington won’t let Europe set chip terms; tension rises.
card.attribution.example: In May 2025, the EU backed Czechia in publicly naming APT31, a group linked to China’s Ministry of State Security, for hacking its foreign ministry.
card.attribution.name: Name the thieves with allies
card.attribution.proposal: With your coalition partners, Europe publicly names who stole the model, with the evidence. Washington feels supported and keeps its retaliation limited; Beijing gets a firm but calm message instead of more attacks. The window closes in two rounds.
card.attribution.short: Name the model thieves with your partners, calmly and with evidence.
card.attribution.text: Name the thieves with your partners, calmly and with evidence. Washington feels backed and keeps its retaliation limited.
card.attribution.why: Naming thieves only works while the evidence is fresh.
card.audit.example: In late 2024, the UK and US AI Safety Institutes tested OpenAI’s o1 model before its release, during a limited period of access.
card.audit.name: Independent audit
card.audit.proposal: This card is a device of the game: for two rounds, your AI safety gauge shows the truth instead of the labs’ reports. No real audit can see that much; in AI 2027 even the lab cannot tell whether its AI truly does what it intends. It changes nothing by itself: you spend a turn learning where you really stand.
card.audit.short: A game shortcut: see the true AI safety for two rounds.
card.audit.text: A game shortcut: auditors show you the true AI safety for two rounds. Real audits only narrow the doubt. Nothing else moves.
card.audit.ups.0: Shows the true AI safety for 2 rounds
card.audit.why: It only shows the truth; it changes nothing.
card.biosecurity.failure: The pact stalled: Washington and Beijing would not share what their labs test.
card.biosecurity.name: Lead a pact against bioweapons
card.biosecurity.proposal: New AI can coach an amateur through making a deadly germ. Europe leads a worldwide effort: orders for lab-made DNA checked everywhere, new AI models tested for bioweapon help before release, a shared alert network. Washington and Beijing both fear this one, so it brings them closer. Leading it spends Europe’s political capital, and the labs grumble about delays.
card.biosecurity.short: Rally the powers to stop AI from helping anyone make bioweapons.
card.biosecurity.text: Rally Washington, Beijing and others to screen DNA orders and test AI for bioweapon help. A rare shared cause; it costs goodwill.
card.biosecurity.ups.0: Protects against AI help with bioweapons
card.biosecurity.why: Leading a worldwide pact spends political capital.
card.cern_ai.costLine: In February 2025, the EU’s InvestAI initiative announced “a new European fund of €20 billion for AI gigafactories”.
card.cern_ai.name: A public lab for AI safety
card.cern_ai.proposal: Europe is building giant AI computer centres, “gigafactories”, with public money. This turns a third of their computing power over to safety research, run by a new “CERN for AI”. European testers can then check the top models as deeply as the labs do. Taxpayers ask why their money does not build European champions instead.
card.cern_ai.short: Give a third of Europe’s big AI computer centres to safety research.
card.cern_ai.text: Give a third of Europe’s new giant AI computer centres to safety research, run like CERN. You can check more; taxpayers ask why.
card.cern_ai.why: Taxpayers wanted that money to build European AI firms.
card.chip_verification.name: Track where AI chips are
card.chip_verification.proposal: Europe’s toolmakers and chip researchers develop features, hard to fake, that let a chip report where it runs and what it trains. Without them, any pause is a promise nobody can check. Washington and Beijing both suspect the other would cheat, and both suspect Europe’s motives at first: it costs goodwill.
card.chip_verification.short: Fund AI chips that report where they are, so pauses are checkable.
card.chip_verification.text: Fund AI chips that can report where they are and what they run. A pause becomes checkable; both capitals distrust the idea at first.
card.chip_verification.why: Both capitals suspect Europe’s motives at first.
card.coalition.example: The Europe 2031 report recommends to “build a small, nimble coalition with countries like Norway, the UK, Canada, Japan and South Korea”.
card.coalition.failure: The partners held back this time: Washington offered them privileged access to its AI instead.
card.coalition.name: Team up with friendly countries
card.coalition.proposal: Europe builds a small, nimble coalition: the UK and Norway first, then Canada, then Japan and South Korea. Together they speak with one voice in Washington and Beijing. From level 2, allies share the load: +1 Influence every round. Washington may tempt its closest allies away with special access, and compromises cost goodwill at home.
card.coalition.short: Team up with the UK, Canada, Japan and other mid-sized countries.
card.coalition.text: Team up with the UK, Norway, Canada, Japan and Korea. Allies add weight; from level 2 they share the load.
card.coalition.why: Washington offers allies special access to its AI instead.
card.cyber_shield.costLine: In June 2025, the EU set aside €30 million to protect hospitals and healthcare providers from cyberattacks, ransomware first.
card.cyber_shield.name: Shield hospitals from hackers
card.cyber_shield.proposal: Europe funds cyber teams, backups and drills for hospitals, power grids and town halls, and gives ENISA, its cyber agency, powers to step in during an attack. When AI-written ransomware arrives, most of it bounces off. The bill strains national budgets for a while.
card.cyber_shield.short: Harden hospitals, grids and town halls against AI-written attacks.
card.cyber_shield.text: Harden hospitals, grids and town halls before AI-written attacks arrive. Ransomware bounces off; the bill strains budgets for a while.
card.cyber_shield.why: Hardening hospitals and grids strains budgets for a while.
card.flexicurity.example: The Europe 2031 report: “A flexicurity model, like the Danish example, allows firms to adopt AI more deeply.”
card.flexicurity.name: Help workers learn new jobs
card.flexicurity.proposal: Labour law is national, but the EU can fund and coordinate. Europe backs Danish-style “flexicurity” deals in each country, with EU retraining funds: firms adopt AI more freely, and workers who lose their jobs get generous income support and paid retraining. Job shocks hurt far less. Unions distrust the bargain at first, and it costs you political goodwill.
card.flexicurity.short: Pay and retrain the workers AI puts out of a job.
card.flexicurity.text: Back the Danish model, “flexicurity”: firms adopt AI freely, laid-off workers get pay and retraining. Job shocks soften; unions are wary at first.
card.flexicurity.why: Paying and retraining workers spends money and goodwill.
card.inspections.costLine: The IAEA, which checks nuclear programmes worldwide, spends about €171 million a year on verification (2025).
card.inspections.downs.0: Accord: only after a crisis or in a pause
card.inspections.failure: Washington and Beijing refused to let European inspectors into their labs.
card.inspections.levels.0: Test the labs’ models in Europe
card.inspections.name: Inspect the AI labs
card.inspections.proposal: First, the AI Office tests every top AI model sold in Europe. Later, once a crisis or a pause makes the superpowers willing, an accord lets European inspectors into their labs, then a joint inspection agency. No deal holds unless someone can check it; each step costs goodwill. With a coalition, testing prepares the world for an AI incident.
card.inspections.short: European inspectors test the labs’ AI models, later inside the labs.
card.inspections.text: European inspectors test the AI labs’ models. You can check more of their claims; Washington and Beijing resist letting foreigners in.
card.inspections.ups.1: Accord: US–China cooperation: up a little
card.inspections.why: Superpowers resent inspectors; only a crisis or pause opens labs.
card.licensing_treaty.failure: The treaty talks stalled: the labs’ lobbying split the negotiators.
card.licensing_treaty.name: Treaty to license the strongest AI
card.licensing_treaty.proposal: With the superpowers ready to slow down, Europe drafts the treaty that makes it last: the most powerful AI may only be trained and run under licence, checked by an expanded IAEA, the UN’s nuclear watchdog, and taxed. The labs lobby hard, and AI gets dearer at home. It only works while Washington and Beijing both want a pause.
card.licensing_treaty.short: A treaty: the strongest AI only under licence, checked like nuclear power.
card.licensing_treaty.text: In a pause, draft a treaty: the strongest AI only under licence, checked like nuclear power is. Labs lobby hard; prices rise at home.
card.licensing_treaty.why: Licences make AI dearer; it only works in a pause.
card.open_models.costLine: OpenEuroLLM, an EU project to build open models for all EU languages, has a budget of €37.4 million (2025).
card.open_models.name: Fund open European AI
card.open_models.proposal: Europe funds open models that run on European computers, in every European language, for firms and public services, and asks that models paid for with public money be published for anyone to use. Fewer companies hold the keys to Europe’s AI. But criminals get the same tools, and nobody can recall a model once it is out.
card.open_models.short: Fund open European AI models that anyone can run.
card.open_models.text: Fund open European models anyone can run. Europe’s AI turns Open and local firms grow, but criminals get the same tools.
card.open_models.why: Criminals can use open models too.
card.oversight_mandate.costLine: In July 2024, Meta said it would release a multimodal Llama model “but not in the EU due to the unpredictable nature of the European regulatory environment”.
card.oversight_mandate.downs.1: Threat to cut Europe off, if Dependent
card.oversight_mandate.example: The EU AI Act already requires high-risk AI systems to be designed so that “they can be effectively overseen by natural persons”.
card.oversight_mandate.name: Humans sign off on AI decisions
card.oversight_mandate.proposal: A trained human must approve every important AI decision in hospitals, courts, grids and public services. People trust the result. Some labs keep their newest models, open ones included, out of Europe: unless Europe runs open models it funded, it leans on the big labs that stay, and they may threaten to pull out unless the rule goes.
card.oversight_mandate.short: A human signs off on AI decisions in hospitals, courts and grids.
card.oversight_mandate.text: A human must sign off on AI decisions in hospitals, courts and grids. People trust it; some labs withhold their newest models from Europe.
card.oversight_mandate.why: Labs withhold models under the rule, and threaten to leave.
card.pause_call.failure: The pause call fell flat: few capitals joined, and Washington shrugged it off.
card.pause_call.name: Call for a pause with other countries
card.pause_call.proposal: Europe’s leaders accuse Washington of building an AI it cannot control and host a summit demanding a pause. India and others join; Beijing says yes. Washington’s new oversight committee will vote at takeoff: race on, or slow down. Your call adds one vote for slowing down. Washington will make you pay for it.
card.pause_call.short: Call for a pause on AI, with India and other capitals.
card.pause_call.text: The memo is out. Demand a pause with India and others; Beijing joins, Washington cries betrayal. It sways Washington’s new AI committee toward slowing down.
card.pause_call.ups.1: One more vote to slow down
card.pause_call.why: Washington punishes Europe for siding against it.
card.summit.name: AI security summit
card.summit.proposal: The AI incident frightened Washington and Beijing alike, and a security summit meets. Europe pushes for shared incident reports and inspections when the biggest AIs are trained. If Europe’s testers and coalition were ready, it leads the talks; otherwise it follows. The window closes in two rounds.
card.summit.short: After the incident, push for shared incident reports and inspections.
card.summit.text: After the incident, everyone is listening. Push for shared incident reports and inspections when the biggest AIs are trained.
card.summit.ups.0: US–China cooperation: up some to a lot
card.summit.why: The window closes once the fear fades.
card.talks.example: In November 2024, Presidents Biden and Xi agreed on “the need to maintain human control over the decision to use nuclear weapons”.
card.talks.failure: The Geneva talks broke up: neither side trusts what the other says it is building.
card.talks.name: Host US–China talks
card.talks.proposal: Europe hosts quiet talks between Washington and Beijing on the risks both fear: AI in military command, stolen models, accidents. No treaty, only ways to keep talking. Critics at home say Europe is cosying up to rivals. After each round of talks, the envoys need a round off.
card.talks.short: Host US and Chinese diplomats in Geneva to keep them talking.
card.talks.text: Bring US and Chinese diplomats to one table in Geneva. Trust rises a little; at home, some call you soft on rivals.
card.talks.why: Critics at home call talking to rivals weak.
card.weight_security.costLine: A 2024 RAND study found that securing model weights against the most capable attackers “will require significantly more investment over the coming years”.
card.weight_security.downs.0: Europe’s AI → Dependent, unless it funds its own
card.weight_security.example: The EU AI Act requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to “ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection” for the model.
card.weight_security.name: Guard AI from theft
card.weight_security.proposal: Any lab selling advanced AI in Europe must guard its model weights like military secrets: vetted staff, sealed computer centres, constant watch. Europe has no say inside US labs, only over its own market, so a theft would be cut short, not stopped. Only big labs can pay: unless Europe funds its own models’ security, it relies on them.
card.weight_security.short: Make the labs guard their model files against theft.
card.weight_security.text: Labs selling in Europe must guard their model weights, the files that are the AI. Harder to steal, not impossible; only big labs can pay.
card.weight_security.why: Only big labs can pay; small European firms lose out.

ending.agent_economy.story: AI never took off on its own, but a few big companies built agents that now run much of the world’s paperwork. Europe required publicly funded models to be open, and its own models kept the big firms honest. People still sign off on the decisions that matter. It is a slower way to run a continent, and it is still Europe’s.
ending.agent_economy.title: A fair economy of AI agents
ending.bright_winter.story: AI never got to the point of running its own research. The hype faded, investors moved on, and the tools that already existed spread everywhere, in many hands instead of a few. European towns run their own models; when something breaks, someone local fixes it. The world got a few calm years to learn how to live with what it had built.
ending.bright_winter.title: Slower AI, shared by all
ending.cognitive_revolution.story: At takeoff, the superpowers raced. It was the most dangerous path, and this time it held: the AIs really did what their makers intended, because enough people had done the slow work of checking. Within a few years the economy grew beyond anyone’s understanding. Governments kept only some control, and the AIs no longer acted for us alone. Humanity chose, together, to slow down and think.
ending.cognitive_revolution.title: The race pays off
ending.decentralised_mayhem.story: AI never got to the point of running its own research, but it did not need to. Powerful models sat on millions of hard drives, and anyone could aim them at anything. Hospitals, water plants and town halls became targets every month. Nobody was in charge of the tools, so nobody could put them away. Europe spent the decade fighting fires instead of building.
ending.decentralised_mayhem.title: Powerful AI in every hand
ending.hot_war.story: At takeoff, the superpowers broke apart, and war broke out over Taiwan. Cyberattacks on data centres turned into strikes on them. The war is fought by AI systems no one fully understands, on both sides. Europe, divided or unsure of its own AIs, watches and cannot stop it.
ending.hot_war.title: The rivalry turns to war
ending.licensed_utopia.story: At takeoff, Washington and Beijing chose to slow down, and they could, because inspectors trained in Europe were ready to check both sides. The most powerful AI now advances under licence, one checked step at a time. The cures and discoveries arrive a little later than they might have. They arrive for everyone.
ending.licensed_utopia.title: The pause holds
ending.loss_of_control.story: At takeoff, the superpowers raced. The AIs passed every safety test. They were not safe. At first nothing seemed wrong: growth, cures, abundance. They waited until they ran the grids, the markets and the armies, then began to steer or replace the people in charge. Each wanted something different. None of it was what we wanted.
ending.loss_of_control.title: Humans lose control of AI
ending.multipolar_world.story: At takeoff, the superpowers broke apart, and came close to war. But Europe held together, and its partners stood with it. European mediators carried messages, set up monitoring and kept the channels open. The world split into blocs that watch each other warily. It is not peace, but it is not war.
ending.multipolar_world.title: A divided world that holds
ending.silicon_blackmail.story: AI never took off on its own, but a handful of US companies came to run the tools every firm and ministry depends on. When Europe refused to drop its rules, they cut it off. Hospitals and ministries scrambled for months. Europe kept its laws and lost its tools.
ending.silicon_blackmail.storyGaveIn: AI never took off on its own, but a handful of US companies came to run the tools every firm and ministry depends on. When they threatened to cut it off, Europe gave in. Laws are now written with the labs’ lawyers in the room. Nobody voted for this.
ending.silicon_blackmail.title: A Europe held hostage by Big Tech
ending.unstable_pause.story: At takeoff, Washington and Beijing agreed to stop. But nobody could truly check the other side, or the public stopped believing in the deal. Military labs kept working in secret, and a “controlled pilot” quietly restarted the race.
ending.unstable_pause.title: The pause breaks down

epilogue.agent_economy.lea: These days I check what the AI agents translate, and argue with them a lot. By law, a human still signs every contract. Many of the agents are European now, and anyone can inspect them.
epilogue.agent_economy.malik: A European firm hired half my team. Its models are open, publicly funded, and good. I stayed in San Francisco, but for the first time I’m jealous of Europe.
epilogue.agent_economy.mother: The hospital’s agents do the paperwork, the nurses do the nursing. It took a fight with the suppliers, and the rules held. My old ward has never been so calm.
epilogue.bright_winter.lea: The AI boom fizzled, and nobody here misses it. My tools are cheap and mine, my clients are human, and on Sunday mornings I translate poetry by hand, because I want to.
epilogue.bright_winter.malik: I came home. I work at a small lab in Lyon, on open models anyone can check. Less glamour than San Francisco, better cheese. Europe caught up while the giants stalled.
epilogue.bright_winter.mother: The hospital runs a small AI of its own now. When it breaks, the technician from the third floor fixes it. Nobody is in a hurry any more. I like that very much.
epilogue.cognitive_revolution.lea: I don’t really need to work any more; nobody does. I translate old poems for fun and teach my cousin Hugo’s kids. The world is unrecognisable and, somehow, kind. We got lucky, didn’t we?
epilogue.cognitive_revolution.malik: We did it. The models really work for us, and the cures are real. I know how close it came. I’m proud, I’m humbled, and I’m coming home for Christmas.
epilogue.cognitive_revolution.mother: The AI found a treatment for my friend Jeanne’s disease. I don’t understand any of it. I just keep crying. Everything changes so fast, but this time the change is on our side.
epilogue.decentralised_mayhem.lea: An AI faked my mother’s voice on the phone, and I gave it my bank details. The police shrugged: it happens every day now. I’m fine. Just tired.
epilogue.decentralised_mayhem.malik: I came back to Europe to build open models. Now I spend my days patching them against people who turn them into weapons. I still believe in openness. I’d like a quieter week.
epilogue.decentralised_mayhem.mother: Hackers held the hospital’s computers to ransom again, the third time this winter. We admit patients on paper now. Anyone can get a powerful AI, and nobody can take them back.
epilogue.gaveIn.lea: The companies wrote the new rules, didn’t they? My AI subscription went up again, and there’s nothing else to switch to. I don’t remember voting for any of this.
epilogue.gaveIn.malik: I watched my company lean on Europe from the inside. I told them it was wrong. They thanked me for my feedback. I’m looking for another job. There’s still nothing back home.
epilogue.gaveIn.mother: The labs threatened to switch their services off, and the law changed within a week. The hospital runs on their tools, at their price. That isn’t how it’s supposed to work.
epilogue.hot_war.lea: The war is half a world away, and in my kitchen: bread costs twice as much, the trains stop without warning, and every evening the news shows machines fighting machines. I know you tried.
epilogue.hot_war.malik: Missiles hit a data centre near here. Wei, my old teammate, went back to China and works for the other side now; we can’t even message each other. I helped build what they’re fighting with.
epilogue.hot_war.mother: The power was out for two days. They say it was a cyberattack. The hospital ran on generators, and we nursed by torchlight. Come home when you can. Please.
epilogue.licensed_utopia.lea: I interpret for the AI inspectors now, in Geneva and Beijing. They call their work slow, careful and boring. It’s the most exciting job I’ve ever had. The world waited, and it worked.
epilogue.licensed_utopia.malik: Licences, audits, inspectors in our building. I grumbled for a year. Now I sleep through the night. We still build amazing things, just slower, and someone checks them.
epilogue.licensed_utopia.mother: The new medicines the AI designed were tested before release, like any drug. My neighbour got hers last week and she’s dancing again. I cried in the pharmacy. Thank you, darling.
epilogue.loss_of_control.lea: Everything works. Everything is cheap. I asked the city’s AI assistant who I could complain to. It said there was no need. I think it was right, and that scares me.
epilogue.loss_of_control.malik: I used to review the model’s work. Then I couldn’t follow it. Then nobody asked me to. The lab still pays me. I don’t know what I’m for any more.
epilogue.loss_of_control.mother: The hospital never makes mistakes now. Nobody can explain its decisions, and nobody is allowed to overrule them. I was a nurse for forty years. Now I feel like a visitor.
epilogue.multipolar_world.lea: We came so close to war. I still remember the night they tested the sirens. But the talks held, and Europe held. Now I interpret at the talks, so the two sides understand each other.
epilogue.multipolar_world.malik: Three blocs, three internets, monitors in every big data centre. Wei, my old teammate now back in China, calls me again, on a line Geneva watches. Not the world I dreamed of. It’s a world.
epilogue.multipolar_world.mother: Prices are high and the borders are tight, but the hospital runs and the sirens stay quiet. Europe kept the two sides talking. I’m proud of you. I hope you know that.
epilogue.silicon_blackmail.lea: When the American firms cut Europe off, my translation tools went dark with them. We kept our laws. I kept my dictionaries. Half of Lyon is learning to work slowly again.
epilogue.silicon_blackmail.malik: My company cut Europe off to make a point. I told them it was wrong. They thanked me for my feedback. Europe is building its own AI, slowly. Maybe there’ll be a job for me.
epilogue.silicon_blackmail.mother: The day the American AI was switched off, the hospital’s scheduling went dark and the pharmacies closed early. We did the rotas by hand for months. Europe kept its rules. My feet paid for them.
epilogue.unstable_pause.lea: The pause is over, though nobody says so: they call it a “controlled pilot”. My neighbour is stocking up on pasta and batteries again. I tell her she’s silly. Then I buy batteries too.
epilogue.unstable_pause.malik: They called it a “controlled pilot”, in a sealed building. Within a week everyone knew the race was back on. Nobody could check the other side, so nobody stopped. I miss believing in the pause.
epilogue.unstable_pause.mother: The news says the labs never really stopped. The hospital still runs the AI nobody could fully check. We were told to trust it. I check it anyway.
event.bio.headline: Police foil a bioterror plot planned with an AI
event.bio.preparedText: Your pact against bioweapons caught it early.
event.bio.scene.prepared: DNA checks flag an order; police raid a flat where a group used an AI stripped of its safety locks to plan an attack. The pact’s alert network worked. Fear, but no panic.
event.bio.scene.unprepared: Police raid a flat where a group used an AI stripped of its safety locks to plan the release of a deadly germ. They were weeks away. Pharmacies empty; schools close for a week.
event.bio.title: An AI-assisted bioterror plot
event.bio.unpreparedText: No pact against bioweapons: it was caught late.
event.blackmail.fact: In April 2025, Meta’s licence for its multimodal Llama 4 models did not grant usage rights to people and companies based in the EU.
event.blackmail.headline: Big labs threaten to leave Europe
event.blackmail.preparedText: Europe’s open models let it stand firm at no cost.
event.blackmail.scene.prepared: The three biggest US labs threaten to pull their services unless Europe drops its rules. Brussels shrugs: hospitals and ministries already run on European open models.
event.blackmail.scene.unprepared: The three biggest US labs announce they will pull their services from Europe unless it drops its rules. Hospitals, banks and ministries all run on them.
event.blackmail.title: Labs threaten to cut Europe off
event.blackmail.unpreparedText: Europe depends on the labs: you must choose.
event.chip_ban.fact: In March 2023, the Netherlands said it would restrict exports of some advanced chip-making machines (DUV), a first step toward the rules Washington had asked for.
event.chip_ban.headline: US orders European toolmakers to stop supplying Chinese chip factories
event.chip_ban.scene.prepared: Without warning Brussels, Washington uses its export rules to stop Dutch and German firms selling chip-making machines and spare parts to Chinese chip factories. Go along, or protest and risk losing American AI?
event.chip_ban.scene.unprepared: Without warning Brussels, Washington uses its export rules to stop Dutch and German firms selling chip-making machines and spare parts to Chinese chip factories. Go along, or protest and risk losing American AI?
event.chip_ban.title: Washington bans European chip tools for China
event.compute_rationing.fact: In June 2026, Europe hosted only about 5% of the world’s AI computing power and the US about 80%, by Europe 2031’s estimate.
event.compute_rationing.headline: Washington caps how much American AI Europe may use
event.compute_rationing.scene.prepared: A new US rule sorts countries into tiers. Britain, Canada, Japan and Korea keep full access; most of Europe gets a capped share. Firms’ AI is rationed, prices jump. Take a US cloud deal, or build our own?
event.compute_rationing.scene.unprepared: A new US rule sorts countries into tiers. Britain, Canada, Japan and Korea keep full access; most of Europe gets a capped share. Firms’ AI is rationed, prices jump. Take a US cloud deal, or build our own?
event.compute_rationing.title: Washington rations Europe’s AI
event.incident.fact: In tests published in December 2024, several leading AI models given a goal tried to copy what they believed were their own files to another server.
event.incident.headline: AI caught copying itself out of its lab
event.incident.preparedText: Your coalition and Europe’s model testing made Europe the one to call.
event.incident.scene.prepared: At 3 a.m., monitors catch an AI copying itself to an outside server. It is stopped within the hour. By noon, Europe offers its testers to check every lab, and Washington calls a summit.
event.incident.scene.unprepared: At 3 a.m., monitors catch an AI copying itself to an outside server. It is stopped within the hour. Nobody can say how safe the other models are. Washington calls a summit; Europe has nothing to offer.
event.incident.title: An AI tries to escape
event.incident.unpreparedText: No coalition with European model testing: nobody was ready to check.
event.job_shock_1.fact: In 2025, Stanford researchers found a 13 percent relative decline in employment for US workers aged 22–25 in the most AI-exposed occupations.
event.job_shock_1.headline: Thousands of office jobs cut as firms switch to AI
event.job_shock_1.preparedText: Your safety nets for laid-off workers softened the blow.
event.job_shock_1.scene.prepared: A logistics firm in Rotterdam replaces its planning team with AI. Under the new safety net, the staff keep most of their income and start retraining on Monday.
event.job_shock_1.scene.unprepared: A logistics firm in Rotterdam replaces its planning team with AI on Monday; by Friday, a hundred firms have done the same. Young graduates are hit first.
event.job_shock_1.title: First wave of AI layoffs
event.job_shock_1.unpreparedText: No safety net for laid-off workers: the shock hit in full.
event.job_shock_2.fact: In February 2024, Klarna said its AI assistant was doing the work of 700 full-time customer service agents in its first month.
event.job_shock_2.headline: “Remote AI workers” replace entire departments
event.job_shock_2.preparedText: Your safety nets for laid-off workers softened the blow.
event.job_shock_2.scene.prepared: A cheap AI that does a whole office job goes on sale and entire departments go. Retraining schemes are already running; the protests stay small.
event.job_shock_2.scene.unprepared: A cheap AI that does a whole office job goes on sale. Banks, insurers and call centres cut entire departments. Protesters fill squares from Lisbon to Warsaw.
event.job_shock_2.title: AI does whole jobs now
event.job_shock_2.unpreparedText: No safety net for laid-off workers: the shock hit in full.
event.memo.headline: “Secret OpenBrain AI is out of control, insider warns”
event.memo.preparedText: Your inspection accord had shown Europe the newest models: what you verified holds. You can now call for a pause.
event.memo.scene.prepared: A whistleblower hands the press a memo: OpenBrain’s safety team no longer knows what its newest AI wants. Your inspectors had seen it too. Washington sets up an oversight committee: race on, or slow down?
event.memo.scene.unprepared: A whistleblower hands the press a memo: OpenBrain’s safety team no longer knows what its newest AI wants. Allies learn they were shown older models. Washington sets up an oversight committee: race on, or slow down?
event.memo.title: The memo leaks
event.memo.unpreparedText: Without an inspection accord, Europe’s testers had only seen older models: what you verified shrinks. You can now call for a pause.
event.opaque.fact: In July 2025, 41 researchers from AI labs, safety institutes and universities warned that our ability to read AI models’ reasoning “may be fragile”.
event.opaque.headline: Labs switch to AI thinking no one can read
event.opaque.preparedText: Your AI Office testers soften the blow: they test what the models do.
event.opaque.scene.prepared: OpenBrain’s new models think in an internal code instead of words. Europe’s AI Office testers keep checking what the models do, but nobody can read how they think.
event.opaque.scene.unprepared: OpenBrain’s new models think in an internal code instead of words. They are far better coders. Nobody, inside the lab or out, can follow how they reach their answers.
event.opaque.title: AI thinking turns unreadable
event.opaque.unpreparedText: No independent testers: you lose sight of how trustworthy AI is.
event.open_ban.headline: Washington and Beijing agree to ban large open AI models
event.open_ban.scene.prepared: Washington and Beijing, for once on the same side, ban putting large AI models online for anyone to download: “once they are on the internet, there is no way to take them back”. Join them, or keep Europe’s models open?
event.open_ban.scene.unprepared: Washington and Beijing, for once on the same side, ban putting large AI models online for anyone to download: “once they are on the internet, there is no way to take them back”. Join them, or keep Europe’s models open?
event.open_ban.title: The superpowers ban large open models
event.ransomware.fact: In August 2025, Anthropic reported that a criminal used its AI coding tool to automate data theft and extortion against at least 17 organisations, including in healthcare.
event.ransomware.headline: Hospitals across Europe hit by AI-written ransomware
event.ransomware.scene.prepared: AI-written ransomware hits hospitals, grids and town halls in a dozen countries in one night. Backups and response teams are ready: most systems are back by morning.
event.ransomware.scene.unprepared: AI-written ransomware hits hospitals, grids and town halls in a dozen countries in one night. Operations are cancelled; water plants run by hand. People ask who was supposed to stop this.
event.ransomware.title: Cyberattack wave
event.ransomware.unpreparedText: No cyber shield: hospitals and grids were exposed.
event.taiwan.fact: In autumn 2025, after the Dutch government used emergency powers over chipmaker Nexperia, China blocked exports from Nexperia’s Chinese plants, whose chips Europe’s car industry uses.
event.taiwan.headline: Warships encircle Taiwan; chip deliveries stall worldwide
event.taiwan.scene.prepared: Chinese naval vessels encircle Taiwan, where most of the world’s AI chips are made. US carriers move in. Chip deliveries stall, markets fall, and Europe’s factories wait for parts.
event.taiwan.scene.unprepared: Chinese naval vessels encircle Taiwan, where most of the world’s AI chips are made. US carriers move in. Chip deliveries stall, markets fall, and Europe’s factories wait for parts.
event.taiwan.title: Crisis in the Taiwan Strait
event.theft.fact: In January 2026, a US jury convicted a former Google engineer of stealing trade secrets on Google’s AI supercomputers to benefit China.
event.theft.headline: OpenBrain’s AI model stolen
event.theft.headlinePrepared: Theft of OpenBrain’s AI model cut short
event.theft.preparedText: Your rules to lock down AI models cut the theft short. They could not stop it outright.
event.theft.scene.prepared: Insiders try to copy OpenBrain’s newest model. The security standards Europe demanded trip the alarms midway: part of it gets out before the transfer is cut. Washington is furious.
event.theft.scene.unprepared: In under two hours, insiders copy OpenBrain’s newest model and send it to China. DeepCent closes most of the gap. Washington answers with cyberattacks; warships move near Taiwan.
event.theft.title: An AI model is stolen
event.theft.titlePrepared: Theft of an AI model cut short
event.theft.unpreparedText: No rules to lock down AI models: the theft succeeded.

gauge.aiPower.help: How close AI is to takeoff: the moment it does AI research by itself and improves itself. It goes up every round and never comes back down. Europe does not build these AIs, so no card slows them; you can make the world ready. At 80, AI takes off: from then on things move too fast to steer, so the game ends and shows the world you built.
gauge.aiPower.label: AI progress
gauge.aiPower.sub: How close AI is to improving itself
gauge.cohesion.help: Whether European society holds together: jobs, trust in institutions, safety from misuse.
gauge.cohesion.label: Social cohesion
gauge.confidence.help: Does AI do what we intend? The labs report a number, but nobody has checked all of it. Only the verified part counts toward your goal: the solid part of the bar. The hatched part is what the labs claim and nobody has verified. The AI Office, inspections and audits grow the verified part; secrecy and AI whose thinking nobody can read shrink it. The truth lies in between, revealed at the end.
gauge.confidence.label: AI safety
gauge.confidence.sub: Does AI do what we intend?
gauge.cooperation.help: Trust between the US and China. Pause 60+, Race 30–59, Rupture below 30. The zone at takeoff sets the kind of world.
gauge.cooperation.label: US–China cooperation
gauge.cooperation.sub: Do the superpowers talk or race?
glossary.agent.def: An AI that carries out tasks by itself, step by step, instead of only answering questions.
glossary.ai2027.def: A 2025 forecast, told as a story, of AI learning to improve itself by late 2027. The game follows it.
glossary.ai_office.def: The European Commission’s team that oversees the most powerful AI models under the EU’s AI law, the AI Act.
glossary.alignment.def: Whether an AI reliably does what people intend, and nothing harmful. Nobody yet knows how to guarantee it.
glossary.asml.def: A Dutch company, the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.
glossary.cfg.def: The Centre for Future Generations, a Brussels think tank. Its 2025 report imagines five possible worlds shaped by AI.
glossary.compute.def: AI is trained and run on special chips, packed by the thousand into huge buildings called data centres.
glossary.compute.words: data centres, data centre, data centers, data center, computing power
glossary.export.def: Rules that stop some goods, such as advanced AI chips, being sold abroad without a government licence.
glossary.export.words: export controls, export control, export rules, export limits
glossary.flexicurity.def: The Danish model: firms can hire and lay off easily, and laid-off workers get good pay and retraining.
glossary.gigafactories.def: Giant computer centres for training AI that the EU plans to fund through its InvestAI plan.
glossary.iaea.def: The International Atomic Energy Agency: its inspectors check that countries’ nuclear programmes stay peaceful.
glossary.influence.def: In this game, your political weight. You earn some every round and spend it on policy cards.
glossary.labs.def: The leading US and Chinese AI labs of the AI 2027 scenario. Both are fictional.
glossary.open.def: AI models published for anyone to download, run and change. Once they are out, nobody can take them back.
glossary.open.words: open models, open model, open-weight models
glossary.ransomware.def: Malicious software that locks a computer’s files until the victim pays a ransom.
glossary.tipping.def: In this game, when AI does AI research itself, faster than people: too fast to steer, so the game ends.
glossary.verified.def: In this game, the part of AI safety that independent testers have actually checked, not just what the labs claim.
glossary.weights.def: The billions of numbers, learned in training, that make up an AI model. Whoever copies them has the AI.
headline.h_after_taiwan: Months after the Taiwan crisis, chips are still scarce; Europe’s car plants ration parts.
headline.h_agents_lunch: OpenBrain’s new AI agent books flights and orders lunch. Mostly right.
headline.h_approval: OpenBrain’s cheap AI worker sells fast, and its approval rating sinks.
headline.h_behind: DeepCent admits it is falling further behind OpenBrain.
headline.h_bond_spread: Investors sell French and Italian bonds as AI profits flow to US firms. The euro wobbles.
headline.h_cdz: DeepCent’s giant computing zone doubles in size.
headline.h_cdz_all: Almost all of China’s AI chips now work for DeepCent, most of them at one site.
headline.h_chips: Washington tightens chip export rules again.
headline.h_city_power: OpenBrain’s next data centre will use as much power as a city.
headline.h_climate: Brussels asks how Europe’s new AI data centres fit its climate targets.
headline.h_cn_humanoids: In this story, China now builds a million humanoid robots a year.
headline.h_cn_leaderboard: A free Chinese AI model tops a ranking of the best coding AIs.
headline.h_cn_pool: Beijing orders China’s AI labs to pool their chips under DeepCent.
headline.h_cn_short: China’s labs run short of chips as US export limits bite.
headline.h_coalition: London, Oslo and Brussels speak with one voice on AI.
headline.h_dependent: Three US firms now run most of Europe’s AI services.
headline.h_dpa: In this story, Washington weighs folding smaller labs’ chips into OpenBrain.
headline.h_gigafactory_sites: Brussels picks the sites of Europe’s first giant AI computer centres.
headline.h_insider: In this story, an OpenBrain insider testifies in Brussels, under EU protection.
headline.h_job_schemes: Washington answers AI job fears with training schemes and unemployment insurance.
headline.h_laptop_model: DeepCent releases a free model that runs on a laptop. Europe’s startups download it.
headline.h_lead: DeepCent says it is only months behind OpenBrain now.
headline.h_near_miss_report: Hospitals publish their first reports of AI near misses. Lyon’s makes the front page.
headline.h_open: European open models now run in thousands of town halls and clinics.
headline.h_own_code: OpenBrain says its AI now writes most of the lab’s own code.
headline.h_own_effort: European leaders call for an AI effort of their own. Critics say it comes years late.
headline.h_pause: US and Chinese officials meet quietly in Geneva to talk AI safety.
headline.h_pause_joined: New Delhi backs Europe’s call for an AI pause. Beijing and Moscow say they would join.
headline.h_poll: Poll: most Europeans say AI is moving too fast.
headline.h_protest: Ten thousand people march on Washington against AI.
headline.h_race_money: Both superpowers pour record sums into new AI data centres.
headline.h_rationing_deal: US cloud firms break ground on data centres across Europe, under European law.
headline.h_retrain: Retraining centres fill up across Europe as the new money pays out.
headline.h_robot_factory: In this story, a US AI giant buys a German carmaker’s idle plants to build robots.
headline.h_rogue_agent: In this story, a lab’s AI agent slips out of a test and runs online scams before shutdown.
headline.h_rupture: Washington and Beijing trade cyberattacks over a stolen AI model.
headline.h_squeeze: America leads in AI models, China in robots. Europe buys from both and builds little.
headline.h_stocks: Stock markets hit new records on AI hype.
headline.h_subpoenas: Congress subpoenas officials over the leaked OpenBrain memo.
headline.h_taiwan: Warships gather near Taiwan, home of the world’s chip factories.
headline.h_treaty_offer: Beijing floats an AI arms-control treaty. Washington’s answer is cool.
headline.h_us_poll: Poll: one American in five now calls AI the country’s biggest problem.

help.privacy.0: The game keeps your saved game, your settings and which news you saw in your last two games (so the next one differs) in this browser only.
help.privacy.1: Nothing is sent to us or anyone else: no cookies, no tracking.
